data.gender_notes: Albemarle is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Old French, Albemarle is composed of two elements: Albe, meaning noble or bright, and marle, meaning famous or renowned. This name was commonly used in the Middle Ages and was brought to America by early settlers. The name Albemarle carries the meaning “Noble, bright one” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Albemarle usually hope their child will grow to embody noble, bright one and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Albemarle total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Albemarle has historical significance in the United States, particularly in the state of North Carolina. The Albemarle Sound, a large body of water in the eastern part of the state, was named after the English Earl of Albemarle, who was the proprietor of the region during the late 17th century. Additionally, Albemarle County in Virginia was named after the earl as well.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Albemarle holds spiritual significance as a reminder of the noble and renowned nature of God. The name, which means "noble, bright, and renowned," is a reflection of the divine qualities of God, who is described in the Bible as being wise, powerful, and holy. Moreover, the name Albemarle can be a source of inspiration and encouragement for believers, reminding them of the noble and bright character of God, and the renowned nature of His love and salvation.
